chapter: Johnny Hammond, Dreams and moving to New York
title: His parents and not finishing Berklee
summary: His parents never fully understood his career or accepted that he left Berklee without a degree.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Did your parents become comfortable with your choice of living eventually?

Eventually they did but it took a long time I think. I don’t know if it ever really quite sunk in, you know, because they’d always say well why don’t you — can’t you go back — because I didn’t quite finish Berklee. I didn’t get the degree, the music ed degree. And they said, “Can’t you go back to Berklee and finish and get that?” And I said no, no, I’m working now. And it sort of reminds me of like, there was one Woody Allen movie where his parents come on at the very end, I forget which one it is, and they are saying, “Ve don know, I mean he could have been a lawyer, he could have done that, look vhat he did vis his life.” You know, and then we’re talking about someone who’s ridiculously successful doing exactly what he wants to do, but I think parents never let go of that somehow. But luckily, what I always appreciated was that even though they had no idea what I wanted to do, they let me at least pursue it. And when they saw I was making a living they just said fine. I think in their own way they were proud of what I did but they never really understood the music. But that’s okay. I’m not sure I do sometimes.
